root_idea.summary: The root centers on returning or turning back, especially a deliberate return toward a prior place, state, or direction.
root_idea.development: From the basic notion of return, the evidence extends to restoring a hand or limb, repeated movement in travel, a destination or abode of return, repentance and repeated turning toward God, and echoing or repeating praise. The Quran-focused discussion distinguishes أَوْبٌ as a voluntary return by an agent with will from the broader notion of return.

Distinct Quranic verbal noun meaning return.

Distinct Quranic noun denoting return or the destination of return.

senses.definition: To repeat or echo praises of God.
senses.usage_conditions: Quranic imperative addressed to the mountains in conjunction with David. A transmitted alternative reading understands the construction as returning with him in repeated praise rather than echoing his praise.
In the Quranic occurrence, the return of people to God is intended. The form denotes the act of returning rather than a place of return.

senses.definition: One who repeatedly turns back to God through repentance and obedience.
senses.usage_conditions: The repeated return may involve leaving sin, resuming obedience, seeking forgiveness, and remaining mindful of God's ordinances.

A transmitted religious explanation uses the form for a praiser of God, including in the expression صلاة الأوابين; this is distinct from the more general description of repeated repentance and obedience.

senses.definition: Return, or the place and destination to which one returns; a return-abode.
senses.usage_conditions: In Quranic contexts it can denote an ultimate destination or final abode, whether favorable or unfavorable, as well as the act or prospect of return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return to a place, person, or thing, or to return from a journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The basic intransitive verb of return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come or return to one's family, people, or the water at night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional temporal construction; some accounts specify the beginning of the night.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To return from disobedience to obedience; to repent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with return from sin or offense, including the construction آبَ إِلَى اللهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the sun, to set or return to its setting place.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The setting is understood figuratively as the sun's return to the place from which it began its course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come to someone from every direction or quarter.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A construction describing people arriving from all sides.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make someone or something return; to put a hand back to a sword, bow, or arrow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive use, including restoring a person or object and directing the hand back toward a weapon or projectile.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To journey through the day, sometimes continuing until night; of travelling camels, to vie with one another in pace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The descriptions vary as to whether the journey ends at night, continues through it, or denotes a particular form of travelling-camel competition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of the Syrian month corresponding to August in the old calendar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized calendrical term, unrelated to the ordinary verbal-noun senses in usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The returning or rapid shifting of an animal's fore and hind legs in movement; swiftness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of gait and quick alternation of the limbs, especially in animals.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A right or direct way, direction, course, or tendency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial or figurative direction toward which one proceeds.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A course or manner of acting; a customary mode of conduct.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a person's established way of behaving or customary practice.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A way, road, quarter, tract, side, or place, including a place to which one returns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A spatial noun covering a route, region, side, or destination according to context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-plural, explained by the bees' repeated return to their hive or night shelter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical plural or collective usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The wind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexical usage recorded without a further semantic restriction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A return.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A substantive noun formed from the basic verb of returning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Return from disobedience to obedience; repentance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A religious or moral return from sin.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Speech or language without profit.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Appears in the idiom كلام لا أوبة له.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The legs of a beast.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The singular of أَوْبَاتٌ in a specialized anatomical or zoological usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A noon-day draught or drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate lexical usage from the return noun to which the headword is also cross-referenced.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel quick in shifting her fore and hind legs while moving.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized adjective for rapid animal gait.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Returning; one who returns.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Active participle of آبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The coming of camels to water to drink every night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage describing the regular nightly return of camels to water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place where the sun sets.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized place noun derived from the notion of return.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A day-journey.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used as a measure of travel distance or duration; plural مَآوِبُ is recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel that prevails when vying with another in pace or movement.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun for an animal distinguished by superior travelling speed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The place in a well where water flows back and collects to replenish what has been drawn.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical term for the water's returning collection point in a well.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wind that blows throughout the day or comes at night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source records variant vocalizations and differing temporal descriptions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Returning to one's family at night; coming at night or at the beginning of the night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial description of nocturnal arrival or return.

cautions: The Quranic imperative أَوِّبِ is normalized under the dictionary citation form أَوَّبَ; the supplied Quran surface form remains represented by its QAC location.

A Lane-reported opinion restricts إِيَاب to returning to one's family at night, but the Quran-focused evidence supports the broader meaning of return, so that restriction is not imposed on the Quranic sense.

أَوَّاب is transmitted with both the repentant-returner interpretation and a praiser-of-God interpretation; these are retained as separate Quran-attested senses rather than collapsed into contextual gloss variation.
